title: Attainable nonlinearity values of APN functions
summary: Classify the nonlinearity values attainable by APN vectorial functions and their differential-spectrum functions.

formal_statement.body: For every dimension $n$, determine exactly which values can occur as $\operatorname{NL}(F)$ for a general APN function $F:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2^n$, and consequently which values can occur as $\operatorname{NL}(\gamma_F)$. In particular, decide whether odd APN nonlinearity values are possible.

scope.domain: APN vectorial Boolean functions and the Boolean differential-spectrum function $\gamma_F$
assumptions: $\gamma_F$ is defined from the differential spectrum
scope.unresolved_remainder: Corollary 3.7 of the later Sidon-set work rules out nonlinearity 1 for APN functions in every dimension n at least 3. A complete attainable-value classification for every n, including the remaining odd-value cases, is still open.

citations.label: Beneteau et al., quadratic APN amplitude constraints

progress.summary: The TIT source explicitly states this unresolved problem and fixes its mathematical scope.
Corollary 3.7 proves L(F) at most 2^n - 4 for every APN function with n at least 3, equivalently excluding APN nonlinearity 1, but it does not classify the remaining attainable values.

Theorems IV.5 and IV.6 restrict the possible amplitude distributions of quadratic APN functions in dimensions eight and ten, giving subclass and finite-dimensional constraints rather than a general attainable-value classification.
citation_labels: Beneteau et al., quadratic APN amplitude constraints
